# Data sets {#sec-data-sets}

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

library(rebook)
chapterPreamble(cache = FALSE)
```

The examples in this book use a small number of public data sets, so that
the same data can be followed across chapters. This appendix gives a short
overview of each data set, the original study and the chapters where it is
used. Most of the data sets are distributed in R packages, whose
documentation describes the data in detail, including the available
variables; follow the links below for these details. For other sources of
open data, see [@sec-example-data].

| Data set | Data | Package | Used in |
|:---------|:-----|:--------|:--------|
| [GlobalPatterns](#sec-data-globalpatterns) | 16S rRNA, 26 samples from 9 environments | mia | many chapters |
| [enterotype](#sec-data-enterotype) | Shotgun metagenomics and 16S rRNA, 280 human fecal samples | mia | [@sec-community-similarity] |
| [peerj13075](#sec-data-peerj13075) | 16S rRNA, skin of 58 individuals | mia | [@sec-correlation], [@sec-clustering] |
| [Tengeler2020](#sec-data-tengeler2020) | 16S rRNA, 27 humanized mice | mia | [@sec-assay-transform], [@sec-differential-abundance] |
| [HintikkaXOData](#sec-data-hintikka) | Microbiota, metabolites and biomarkers, 40 rats | mia | multi-omics chapters |
| [hitchip1006](#sec-data-hitchip1006) | HITChip microarray, 1006 adults | miaTime | [@sec-mediation] |
| [peerj32](#sec-data-peerj32) | HITChip microarray and serum lipids, 22 subjects, 2 time points | microbiomeDataSets | [@sec-time-diversity] |
| [baboongut](#sec-data-baboongut) | 16S rRNA, 16,234 samples from 585 wild baboons | microbiomeDataSets | [@sec-quality-control] |
| [QinJ_2012](#sec-data-qin2012) | Shotgun metagenomics, 363 human fecal samples | curatedMetagenomicData | [@sec-machine_learning] |
| [HoloFood](#sec-data-holofood) | Biogenic amines and fatty acids, 10 chickens | OMA | [@sec-containers] |

## GlobalPatterns {#sec-data-globalpatterns}

Microbial communities of 23 environmental samples, such as human feces, skin
and tongue, freshwater, ocean and soil, and three mock communities of known
composition, profiled with 16S rRNA gene sequencing [@Caporaso2011]. The data
is the most common example in this book because it covers very different
types of communities. See the
[documentation](https://microbiome.github.io/mia/reference/GlobalPatterns.html)
in `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("mia")`.

```{r}
#| label: data_globalpatterns
#| eval: false

data("GlobalPatterns", package = "mia")
```

## enterotype {#sec-data-enterotype}

Genus-level profiles of 280 human fecal samples, used to define the
enterotypes of the human gut microbiome [@Arumugam2011]. The data combine
shotgun metagenomic sequencing (Sanger and Illumina; 126 samples) and 16S
rRNA gene pyrosequencing (454; 154 samples); the technology is given in
the `SeqTech` column. See the
[documentation](https://microbiome.github.io/mia/reference/enterotype.html)
in `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("mia")`.

```{r}
#| label: data_enterotype
#| eval: false

data("enterotype", package = "mia")
```

## peerj13075 {#sec-data-peerj13075}

Skin microbiota of 58 volunteers from three cities in India, profiled with
16S rRNA gene sequencing, together with information on, for instance, their
age, diet and geographical location [@potbhare2022skin]. See the
[documentation](https://microbiome.github.io/mia/reference/peerj13075.html)
in `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("mia")`.

```{r}
#| label: data_peerj13075
#| eval: false

data("peerj13075", package = "mia")
```

## Tengeler2020 {#sec-data-tengeler2020}

Gut microbiota of 27 germ-free mice that were colonized with stool from
individuals with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) or from
healthy controls, in three cohorts, profiled with 16S rRNA gene sequencing
[@Tengeler2020]. See the
[documentation](https://microbiome.github.io/mia/reference/Tengeler2020.html)
in `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("mia")`.

```{r}
#| label: data_tengeler2020
#| eval: false

data("Tengeler2020", package = "mia")
```

## HintikkaXOData {#sec-data-hintikka}

A multi-omics data set from a diet study with 40 rats, which were fed a
high-fat or a low-fat diet with or without xylo-oligosaccharide prebiotics
[@Hintikka2021]. It is a `MultiAssayExperiment` with three experiments
measured from the same samples: cecal microbiota, NMR metabolites and
biomarkers. See the
[documentation](https://microbiome.github.io/mia/reference/HintikkaXOData.html)
in `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("mia")`. The data is used in the multi-omics chapters
([@sec-global-association], [@sec-cross-correlation] and
[@sec-unsupervised-multiomics]) and in examples on data containers.

```{r}
#| label: data_hintikka
#| eval: false

data("HintikkaXOData", package = "mia")
```

## hitchip1006 {#sec-data-hitchip1006}

Genus-level gut microbiota profiles of 1006 western adults without reported
health complications, measured with the HITChip phylogenetic microarray
[@Lahti2014]. See the
[documentation](https://microbiome.github.io/miaTime/reference/hitchip1006.html)
in `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("miaTime")`.

```{r}
#| label: data_hitchip1006
#| eval: false

data("hitchip1006", package = "miaTime")
```

## peerj32 {#sec-data-peerj32}

Gut microbiota and serum lipid profiles of 22 subjects before and after a
probiotic or placebo intervention [@Lahti2013]. The microbiota was measured
with the HITChip phylogenetic microarray. See the
[documentation](https://microbiome.github.io/microbiomeDataSets/reference/LahtiMLData.html)
in `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("microbiomeDataSets")`.

```{r}
#| label: data_peerj32
#| eval: false

mae <- microbiomeDataSets::peerj32()
```

## baboongut {#sec-data-baboongut}

Longitudinal gut microbiota profiles of wild baboons, 16,234 samples from 585
individuals collected over 14 years, profiled with 16S rRNA gene sequencing
[@Grieneisen2021]. See the
[documentation](https://microbiome.github.io/microbiomeDataSets/reference/GrieneisenTSData.html)
in `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("microbiomeDataSets")`.

```{r}
#| label: data_baboongut
#| eval: false

tse <- microbiomeDataSets::baboongut()
```

## QinJ_2012 {#sec-data-qin2012}

Shotgun metagenomic profiles of fecal samples from Chinese individuals with
type 2 diabetes and healthy controls [@qin2012_t2d], available in
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("curatedMetagenomicData")` [@Pasolli2017]. See its
[documentation](https://waldronlab.io/curatedMetagenomicData/articles/curatedMetagenomicData.html)
for how the data was processed and how to retrieve it; the code is shown in
[@sec-machine_learning].

## HoloFood {#sec-data-holofood}

A small `MultiAssayExperiment` from the HoloFood project, with biogenic amine
and fatty acid profiles from 10 chickens, some of which were sampled at several
time points. It is included in this book's package and is used in
[@sec-containers] to demonstrate how samples are mapped to individuals. More
HoloFood data can be retrieved with `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("HoloFoodR")`.

```{r}
#| label: data_holofood
#| eval: false

mae <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "mae_holofood.Rds", package = "OMA"))
```
